projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained presence of ~26 mobile devices combined with zero camera motion and recent long sleep logs for both adults strongly suggests a large, quiet gathering or sleepover is underway, with cameras likely disabled or guests confined to off-camera areas while the adults slept.

The sustained presence of 25–27 devices alongside zero camera motion late on a Friday strongly indicates a quiet sleepover or guest gathering, which aligns with the household's two pre-teen children and represents normal weekend activity rather than a network anomaly.

The sustained connection of 25–27 mobile devices alongside zero camera motion strongly indicates a quiet house party or gathering is in progress, likely confined to camera-blind zones or using low-light settings that bypass motion detection. This cross-signal pattern confirms a normal Friday evening event rather than a security anomaly, but warrants monitoring for noise or energy spikes.

The sustained presence of 18–26 devices combined with zero camera activity on a Friday evening strongly suggests a social gathering where cameras were intentionally disabled for privacy, which explains the lack of motion alerts and normalizes the network fluctuations.

The sustained fluctuation of 18–26 connected devices paired with zero camera activity strongly indicates Wi-Fi presence detection instability or devices rapidly cycling in/out of range, rather than actual occupancy changes; this could trigger false automations or mask underlying network issues, so verifying router logs or device sleep schedules is recommended.

The sharp drop in connected devices from 25 to 19 between 17:17 and 17:19, paired with zero camera activity, strongly indicates the family is departing the house for the weekend. This suggests transitioning the home to an away/secure state and adjusting climate or pet monitoring routines accordingly.

The sustained fluctuation of 24–27 connected devices paired with zero camera or activity data strongly suggests a network detection anomaly or IoT device spillover rather than actual occupancy, which may be causing false presence triggers for home automations.

The sustained high and unstable mobile device count (24–26) paired with zero camera or activity data strongly indicates a Wi-Fi presence detection glitch or device scanning loop rather than actual occupancy, suggesting a network health issue that could skew presence analytics.

The sustained fluctuation between 21-23 connected devices combined with zero camera or activity data over four hours strongly indicates a network anomaly, such as a rogue access point or IoT device glitch, rather than actual household presence. This warrants a network diagnostic to prevent false automation triggers and ensure Wi-Fi stability.

The sustained high but unstable device count (18–23) paired with zero camera and activity data confirms a Wi-Fi/Bluetooth scanning artifact or IoT reconnection cycle rather than actual occupancy, indicating no security or presence event requires attention.
